title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: Hold: the briefing calls licensing unpublished even though Microsoft documents the underlying Teams events entitlements. It also casts doubt on user external-access policies despite Microsoft's rule that external access requires both organisation and user-policy permission. The revised rollout window is reported correctly.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to add external presenter support to event group chat.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: Event group chat is a private coordination chat for organisers, co-organisers and presenters in events or structured meetings.
claims.quote: the private chat used by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters for coordination during an event or structured meeting.

claims.claim: Presenters outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event will be able to participate in event group chat.
claims.quote: This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

claims.claim: For events optimized for large audiences, the existing event group chat is available before, during and after the event.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.claim: Event group chat is separate from attendee chat, and attendees do not use the event group chat.
claims.quote: Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

go to Meetings > Events policies.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is wholly unpublished or unknown, including whether organisers need a particular licence.
claims.quote: Event capabilities and attendee capacity vary based on the organizer's license.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the broad unpublished-licensing statements in the notes, Cost and licensing, Open questions and cost rationale with: 'Teams events use the organiser's eligible Teams licence; Microsoft documents Teams Enterprise event entitlements. An additional licence, price or meter specific to this external-presenter chat change is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing and the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/plan-events. Keep cost 'low' for the known administrative work; do not claim that external presenters require a particular licence.
